findings.failure_scenario: The added argument claims 'git add -A swept ADR-0036, M4.10b's 208-line deliverable, into this commit TWICE' and 'Caught both times only because a reviewer diffed against the recorded staged_tree'. MEASURED against every recorded artifact, the ADR was swept in ONCE and caught ONCE. (1) .harness/review holds exactly three hashes for M0.79 -- b5232d5c8b40 (staged_tree 73bbbb561fe7b5), b381c73cb0c0 (staged_tree 469567ea8610), 7cadde431155 (staged_tree b18857410502). `git ls-tree -r --name-only <tree> | grep 0036` returns the ADR for 469567ea8610 ONLY; it is absent from 73bbbb561fe7b5 and from b18857410502. (2) The four generated packets agree: /tmp/claude-1000/p079.txt has no ADR line, p079-r2.txt carries it as an ADDITION ('A docs/internal/product/decisions/0036-...'), p079-r3.txt carries it as a DELETION ('-# 0036. The idempotency key carries an explicit pod incarnation'), p079-r4.txt has none. (3) Round 3's two verdicts (7cadde431155.reviewer.json, .test-reviewer.json) are both 'pass' and their five findings -- F8, F9, M0.79-T7, M0.79-T8, M0.79-T9 -- are all about brevity/SKILL.md and reviewer.md; neither mentions the ADR. So one sweep, blocked by both roles at round 2, and round 3 spent re-reviewing after its removal. Even under the charitable reading that a second sweep happened between rounds and was self-caught before a packet existed, the clause 'Caught both times only because a REVIEWER diffed against the recorded staged_tree' is false: exactly one reviewer catch is recorded. The failure this causes: baselines/review.txt is the greppable register a future author and a future reviewer read to calibrate how often the mechanism catches scope creep, and rule two-round-cap's own text ('The number is load-bearing twice', 'at least nine', 'at least 22 tasks') shows this project treats those counts as load-bearing evidence. This entry inflates the review mechanism's catch count by 100% in the one file whose purpose is an honest round record -- and it does so directly beneath the M0.76 entry, whose entire subject is 'FOUR WRONG NUMBERS IN A COMMIT WHOSE SUBJECT IS BOUNDING UNCHECKED PROSE', and beneath the M0.77 row that entry produced, which demands 'quote the method with the number'. No gate can see it: check-archive-row-size.sh caps row LENGTH, check-reviewed.sh requires only that a `rounds:M0.79` line be added with a reason after the key, and neither reads .harness/review. Fix: say the sweep happened once and cost two rounds -- round 2 blocked by both roles on F5/M0.79-T5, round 3 spent re-reviewing after the removal -- or, if a second sweep really occurred, say it was caught by the author before any packet existed, since it is in no artifact.

'Splitting further means committing a skill without the index row that resolves it, or an index row pointing at a file the commit does not carry.' Stated as exhaustive, and it is not. A third seam exists and it is where three of the nine staged files sit: .agents/skills/review/SKILL.md, .claude/agents/reviewer.md and .claude/agents/test-reviewer.md. Commit A = brevity/SKILL.md + .claude/commands/brevity.md + the two generated index rows + the backlog row: build-index.sh --check globs '.agents/skills/*/' in the WORKTREE and reads only the skill frontmatter, so it is green; the adapter points at a skill the same commit carries; check-links.sh resolves. Commit B = the review/SKILL.md paragraph + the two briefs: its only new link target, ../brevity/SKILL.md, exists once A has landed, and none of those three paths feeds any generated index. Neither piece produces a skill with no index row or an index row pointing at an absent file. That seam is also exactly where rounds 1-3 split: F1/M0.79-T2/M0.79-T3 were about the skill body, F3/F6/M0.79-T6/M0.79-T9 about the reviewer wiring. The entry's CONCLUSION survives -- splitting at round 4 costs four fresh rounds and saves none -- but the reason it gives is not the reason, and a future author cites this line to argue that any skill-landing commit is unsplittable when only the skill and its index rows are actually coupled.

'an ADR changing both delta encodings would have landed with no cost review' calls Checkpoint a delta encoding. ADR-0036 changes CommitDelta (line 98, 'carries the full triple PER SegmentCommit') and Checkpoint (line 91, 'not a ChainEntry at all: own MAGIC, own VERSION, no kind'), and line 168 turns Checkpoint.decode into an enumerated {0,1} version set -- a version bump on a non-chain format, not a delta. The M4.10 entry sitting two lines above this one in the same file records that exact conflation as its round-2 defect: 'Checkpoint is not a ChainEntry, and ADR-0033 requires it never decode as one -- so the row forbade the version bump it needs'. Repeating the conflation here means a reader of the M4.10b history reconstructs one format change where there are two of different kinds, which is the error M4.10's own row was rewritten to prevent. Say 'both commit-chain formats' or name them.
